idiom_name: case class copy(...) plus val rebinding (AtomicReference.updateAndGet for shared state)
implementation_notes: Scala models state as immutable case class instances with val fields, so an update is copy(field = newValue): building the replacement is the only fallible work, and publishing it (state = state.copy(...)) is one reference store that cannot fail -- the commit half of the idiom with no swap to write. copy is shallow, so nested mutable collections are still shared and have to be rebuilt; use immutable collections (List, Vector, Map) and construct the changed branch explicitly. For state shared between threads the commit must be atomic: AtomicReference.updateAndGet/compareAndSet is the direct analogue of the non-throwing swap, while a get-then-set pair loses concurrent updates; an actor or a single-writer dispatcher achieves the same by construction.
pitfalls: copy is shallow and only as immutable as the fields: a case class with var fields or mutable collections can still be changed in place, and a var field participates in hashCode while making the instance unsafe as a key.
updateAndGet/compareAndSet may retry their lambda, so it must be pure; two writers using get plus set silently lose one of the updates.
state = state.copy(...) on a var is a plain store, not a publication barrier: without volatile or an atomic reference other threads are not guaranteed to see the new instance.
